title: Clothing and shoes for the weather
summary: How to dress for the ground in sun, heat, cold and rain, which shoes you need on a course and what the dress code of Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting says.

body.html: You spend several hours outdoors at a ground, and in Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ you also walk a course through woods and fields. So your clothes must be comfortable and right for the weather, and above all they must not get in the way of the mount.

The main rule is layers: a thin base T-shirt, a light jumper or fleece over it, the vest on top and, in rain, a light waterproof jacket. You can take layers off and put them back on during the day. Bulky collars, hoods and thick jackets can catch the stock, so check your mount in what you are wearing.

The dress code is the same for everyone in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting. Short shorts are banned; only long shorts are allowed, ending no more than 5 cm above the knee. Tops need at least short sleeves and a collar or a round neck, so sleeveless tops do not work in competition. A vest may not be worn over a bare chest. Details: Dress code and safety on the stand.

Shoes must be closed, with a good grip. Sandals are banned for safety reasons, in Compak® Sporting even in practice. On a Sporting™ course you meet wet grass, mud and slopes, so trail shoes or light boots work well. Shoes must hold your feet steady, because a steady stance helps each shot.
A few practical points: tie long hair back, so that it does not get between your cheek and the stock. Long earrings and necklaces can also get in the way of the mount.

Sun: you may stand in the sun all day. A cap or hat with a peak protects your head and cuts glare, and sunscreen protects the skin of your face, neck and arms. Drink water regularly and find shade between rounds.

Heat: tiredness, dizziness, headache, feeling sick or heavy sweating can be signs of heat exhaustion. Stop shooting, move to a cool, shady place, drink water, cool your skin and tell someone nearby. If there is no improvement within about 30 minutes, or the person becomes confused, call emergency help.

Cold, rain and wind: dress in layers and bring a rain jacket and spare thin gloves. Cold fingers feel the trigger less well, so warm your hands between rounds. A peaked cap keeps rain off your glasses. What to do in a thunderstorm: The core safety rules.

Both rulebooks also set dress for ceremonies. In the opening parade, members of national teams wear the team outfit or smart trousers and a blazer, and prize winners must come to the prize-giving dressed the same way. If you may reach the podium, pack smart trousers and a blazer and check the competition programme. More: Traditions: prize giving, teams and customs.

key_points.html: Dress in layers and check that your clothing does not hamper the mount.
The dress code is the same for all: long shorts ending no more than 5 cm above the knee, sleeves, no sandals.
Closed shoes with a good grip; sandals are banned.
Hair tied back and few accessories near the face.
Cap, sunscreen, water and shade against sun and heat.

did_you_know.html: Many shooters carry spare socks and a T-shirt: after a wet course a dry change can give a real lift for the last rounds.

quiz.q: Which shorts does the FITASC dress code allow?

options.text: Any shorts, as long as they are dark
Long ones, ending 5 cm or less above the knee
No shorts of any kind are allowed
Only shorts made of sports fabric

quiz.explain: Only long, Bermuda-type shorts are allowed, in both disciplines.
Closed shoes protect the feet and give a steady footing.

quiz.q: What should you check after putting on a jacket or jumper?

options.text: Whether its colour suits the vest
Whether the stock catches in the mount
Whether it is in the club's colours

quiz.explain: Bulky clothing can spoil the mount, and with it your shooting.
